LESSON: THE MARKET

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.5: The market
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The market, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have markets?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify roles of people found in a market,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The market in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. list food items found in the market,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The market in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. categorise food items found in the market into fruits and vegetables,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The market in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate activities that are carried out in a market. ● Learners with low vision watch video clips of people found in a market, while learners with blindness listen to audio clips of people found in a market. ● In groups, learners talk about roles of people found in a market and share the information with peers. ● Learners with low vision use flashcards to match fruits found in the market such as bananas, oranges, lemon and vegetables such as spinach, carrots, cabbage. Learners with blindness use braille cards to match fruits found in the market such as bananas, oranges, lemon, vegetables such as spinach, carrots, cabbage. ● Learners with low vision are guided to observe pictures of different fruits and vegetables while learners with blindness are guided to manipulate real fruits and vegetables found in the market. ● Learners with low vision are guided to sort and group food items found in the market into vegetables and fruits using pictures or flashcards. Learners with blindness are guided to use braille cards or real food items to sort them into vegetables and fruits. ● In groups, learners use digital devices with assistive technology to watch pictures of fruits and vegetables found in the market. Learners with Why do we have markets? 11 blindness are guided use digital devices with assistive technology to listen to picture description of fruits and vegetables found in the market. ● In pairs or groups, learners recite poems and sing songs on fruits and vegetables found in the market. Core Competency to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learner listens keenly and speaks effectively when sharing information with peers on roles of people found in a market.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The market together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: A learner enhances cooperation when drawing and colouring different fruits and vegetables found in the market in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social-economic issues: A learner develops the skill of career awareness when drawing and colouring different fruits and vegetables found in

the market.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Food items found in a market relates to concepts of sorting and grouping in Mathematics Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Approved learning support materials, local environment, vegetables, fruits, photographs or picture cut outs of fruits and vegetables, pencils and

crayons, digital devices with assistive technology.
